# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

```plantuml
@startuml

title pa21 Model

class Alive {
    collectedExtraLives : List<Position>
    collectedGems : List<Position>
}
abstract class BoardElement {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
abstract class Cell {
    position : Position
}
class Dead {
    minePosition : Position
}
abstract class Entity {
    owner : EntityCell
    setowner(owner : EntityCell) : EntityCell
}
class EntityCell {
    entity : Entity
    setentity(newEntity : Entity) : Entity
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class ExtraLife {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class GameBoard {
    board : CellArray2D
    numCols : int
    numRows : int
    player : Player
    getCell1(row : int, col : int) : Cell
    getCell2(position : Position) : Cell
    getCol(col : int) : List<Cell>
    getEntityCell1(position : Position) : EntityCell
    getEntityCell2(row : int, col : int) : EntityCell
    getNumGems() : int
    getRow(row : int) : List<Cell>
}
class GameBoardController {
    gameBoard : GameBoard
    makeMove(direction : Direction) : MoveResult
    undoMove(prevMove : MoveResult) : void
}
class GameBoardView {
    gameBoard : GameBoard
    output(useUnicodeChars : boolean) : void

    processMove(direction : Direction) : MoveResult
    processUndo() : boolean
}

    UNLIMITED_LIVES : int
    initialNumOfGems : int
    numDeaths : int
    numLives : int
    numMoves : int

    moveStack : MoveStack

    decrementNumLives() : int
    getGameBoardController() : GameBoardController

    getNumGems() : int
    getScore() : int
    getnumLives() : int

    hasUnlimitedLives() : boolean
    hasWon() : boolean
    increaseNumLives(delta : int) : int
    incrementNumDeaths() : int
    incrementNumMoves() : int
}

    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class Invalid {
}
class Mine {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
abstract class MoveResult {
    newPosition : Position
}
class MoveStack {
    popCount : int
    moves : List<MoveResult>
    isEmpty() : boolean
    peek() : MoveResult
    pop() : MoveResult
    push(move : MoveResult) : void
}
class Player {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class Position {
    col : int
    row : int
    offsetBy1(dRow : int, dCol : int) : Position
    offsetBy2(offset : PositionOffset) : Position
    offsetByOrNull1(dRow : int, dCol : int, numRows : int, numCols : int) : Position
    offsetByOrNull2(offset : PositionOffset, numRows : int, numCols : int) : Position

class PositionOffset {
    dCol : int
    dRow : int
}

    toUnicodeChar() : char

enum Direction {
    UP
    DOWN
    LEFT
    RIGHT
}

The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary: Executes a move for the player in the given direction using inertial sliding mechanics.
Algorithm:
  1. Get player's current position.
  2. Compute delta from direction (UP: (-1,0), DOWN: (1,0), LEFT: (0,-1), RIGHT: (0,1)).
  3. Simulate sliding step-by-step:
     - At each step, compute next position using offsetByOrNull1.
     - If next position is null (out of bounds) -> stop, return Alive (if moved at least one step) or Invalid.
     - Get cell at next position.
     - If cell is Wall -> stop before it, return Alive (if moved) or Invalid.
     - If cell is StopCell -> stop exactly on it, return Alive (if moved) or Invalid.
     - If cell is EntityCell:
       - If entity is Mine -> return Dead with minePosition and original player position.
       - If entity is Gem -> record position in collectedGems list.
       - If entity is ExtraLife -> record position in collectedExtraLives list.
     - Move player to next position (update player's owner cell).
  4. If no steps were taken (first step blocked) -> return Invalid.
  5. After stopping normally, return Alive with collected items and new position.
Related Features: gameBoard, player
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Position, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell, Mine, Gem, ExtraLife
Input: direction - Direction enum (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT)
Output: MoveResult - Alive (with collected items and new position), Dead (with mine position), or Invalid
Pre-condition: gameBoard and player are initialized.
Post-condition: If Alive, player position updated, collected Gems/ExtraLives removed from board, MoveResult contains collected items. If Dead, player position unchanged, board unchanged. If Invalid, nothing changes.

GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverses a previous Alive move by restoring the board state.
Algorithm:
  1. Cast prevMove to Alive.
  2. For each collectedGem position in prevMove: place a Gem entity back in that EntityCell.
  3. For each collectedExtraLife position in prevMove: place an ExtraLife entity back in that EntityCell.
  4. Move player back to prevMove.origPosition.
Related Features: gameBoard, player
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Alive, Position, Gem, ExtraLife, EntityCell
Input: prevMove - the MoveResult (must be Alive) to undo
Output: void
Pre-condition: prevMove is an Alive MoveResult with valid collected item lists and origPosition.
Post-condition: The board state is restored to before the undone move. Player position is restored to origPosition.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top move from the stack, increments popCount.
Algorithm: popCount++; return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1)
Related Features: moves, popCount
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the removed top move
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: The top move is removed from the stack, popCount is incremented by 1.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the move stack is empty.
Algorithm: return moves.isEmpty()
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no moves are in the stack
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns whether the stack is empty.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top move from the stack without removing it.
Algorithm: return moves.get(moves.size() - 1)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the top move on the stack
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: Returns the top MoveResult without modifying the stack.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Adds a move to the top of the stack.
Algorithm: moves.add(move)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move - the MoveResult to push onto the stack
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The move is added to the end of the moves list.

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top move from the stack, increments popCount.
Algorithm: popCount++; return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1)
Related Features: moves, popCount
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the removed top move
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: The top move is removed from the stack, popCount is incremented by 1.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the move stack is empty.
Algorithm: return moves.isEmpty()
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no moves are in the stack
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns whether the stack is empty.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top move from the stack without removing it.
Algorithm: return moves.get(moves.size() - 1)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the top move on the stack
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: Returns the top MoveResult without modifying the stack.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Adds a move to the top of the stack.
Algorithm: moves.add(move)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move - the MoveResult to push onto the stack
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The move is added to the end of the moves list.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Position::offsetBy2
Summary: Creates a new Position offset by a PositionOffset.
Algorithm: return new Position(this.row + offset.dRow, this.col + offset.dCol)
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input: offset - PositionOffset containing dRow and dCol deltas
Output: Position - new position with added deltas
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a new Position with row+offset.dRow and col+offset.dCol.

Position::offsetByOrNull2
Summary: Creates a new Position offset by a PositionOffset, returns null if out of bounds.
Algorithm: newRow = this.row + offset.dRow; newCol = this.col + offset.dCol; if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= numRows || newCol < 0 || newCol >= numCols) return null; return new Position(newRow, newCol)
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input: offset - PositionOffset containing deltas, numRows - total number of rows, numCols - total number of columns
Output: Position - new position if within bounds, null otherwise
Pre-condition: numRows > 0, numCols > 0
Post-condition: Returns a new Position if within bounds, null if out of bounds.

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Creates a new Position offset by given deltas, returns null if out of bounds.
Algorithm: newRow = this.row + dRow; newCol = this.col + dCol; if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= numRows || newCol < 0 || newCol >= numCols) return null; return new Position(newRow, newCol)
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position
Input: dRow - integer delta for row, dCol - integer delta for column, numRows - total number of rows, numCols - total number of columns
Output: Position - new position if within bounds, null otherwise
Pre-condition: numRows > 0, numCols > 0
Post-condition: Returns a new Position if within bounds, null if out of bounds.

Position::offsetBy1
Summary: Creates a new Position offset by given row and column deltas.
Algorithm: return new Position(this.row + dRow, this.col + dCol)
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position
Input: dRow - integer delta for row, dCol - integer delta for column
Output: Position - new position with added deltas
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a new Position with row+ dRow and col+ dCol.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

Algorithm: return !hasUnlimitedLives() && numLives <= 0
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if lives are zero or negative (and not unlimited)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns whether the player has lost.

GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases numLives by the specified delta amount.
Algorithm: numLives = numLives - delta; return new numLives.
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta - positive integer amount to decrease lives by
Output: int - the new numLives value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numLives is decreased by delta.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Calculates and returns the current score based on the formula: Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4), where InitialBoardSize = numRows * numCols, CollectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems().
Algorithm:
  boardSize = gameBoard.numRows * gameBoard.numCols
  collectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems()
  return boardSize + (collectedGems * 10) - (numMoves * 1) - (moveStack.popCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4)
Related Features: gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols, initialNumOfGems, numMoves, numDeaths, moveStack.popCount
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None
Output: int - calculated score
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns score as per formula.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::getnumLives
Summary: Returns the current number of lives.
Algorithm: If numLives < 0, return Integer.MAX_VALUE (unlimited lives). Otherwise return numLives.
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - number of lives (could be Integer.MAX_VALUE for unlimited)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the current lives count.

GameState::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost the game.
Algorithm: return !hasUnlimitedLives() && numLives == 0
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if lives are zero (and not unlimited)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns whether the player has lost.

GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases numLives by the specified delta amount.
Algorithm: numLives = numLives - delta; return new numLives.
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta - positive integer amount to decrease lives by
Output: int - the new numLives value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numLives is decreased by delta.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Calculates and returns the current score based on the formula: Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4), where InitialBoardSize = numRows * numCols, CollectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems().
Algorithm:
  boardSize = gameBoard.numRows * gameBoard.numCols
  collectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems()
  return boardSize + (collectedGems * 10) - (numMoves * 1) - (moveStack.popCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4)
Related Features: gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols, initialNumOfGems, numMoves, numDeaths, moveStack.popCount
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None
Output: int - calculated score
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns score as per formula.

GameState::getGameBoardView
Summary: Creates and returns a new GameBoardView for the current game board.
Algorithm: return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard)
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameBoardView, GameBoard
Input: None
Output: GameBoardView - a view object for displaying the board
Pre-condition: gameBoard is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns a new GameBoardView instance associated with the current board.

GameState::decrementNumLives
Summary: Decreases numLives by exactly 1.
Algorithm: numLives = numLives - 1; return new numLives.
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - the new numLives value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numLives is decreased by 1.

GameState::getNumGems
Summary: Returns the number of Gems remaining on the game board.
Algorithm: return gameBoard.getNumGems()
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameBoard
Input: None
Output: int - number of remaining Gems (>= 0)
Pre-condition: gameBoard is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns the count of Gems still on the board.

GameState::incrementNumMoves
Summary: Increments numMoves by 1.
Algorithm: numMoves = numMoves + 1; return new numMoves.
Related Features: numMoves
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - the new numMoves value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numMoves is incremented by 1.

GameState::hasUnlimitedLives
Summary: Returns true if the player has unlimited lives, i.e., numLives is less than zero.
Algorithm: return numLives < 0
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if unlimited lives, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns true if numLives < 0, false otherwise.

GameState::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has won by collecting all Gems.
Algorithm: return getNumGems() == 0
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameBoard
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no Gems remain on the board
Pre-condition: gameBoard is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns whether the player has won.

GameState::increaseNumLives
Summary: Increases numLives by the specified delta amount.
Algorithm: numLives = numLives + delta; return new numLives.
Related Features: numLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta - positive integer amount to increase lives by
Output: int - the new numLives value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numLives is increased by delta.

GameState::incrementNumDeaths
Summary: Increments numDeaths by 1.
Algorithm: numDeaths = numDeaths + 1; return new numDeaths.
Related Features: numDeaths
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - the new numDeaths value
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: numDeaths is incremented by 1.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

Entity::setowner

Algorithm: Store the current owner, set the new owner, return the previous owner.
Related Features: owner attribute
Related Classes: EntityCell
Input: owner - the new EntityCell that will own this Entity
Output: EntityCell - the previous owner cell (can be null)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The owner attribute is updated to the new owner. The previous owner is returned.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary: Executes a move in the given direction using inertial sliding. Returns Alive, Dead, or Invalid depending on what happens during the slide.
Algorithm:
  1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction.
  2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position).
  3. If the immediate next cell in direction is out of bounds, Wall, or StopCell, return Invalid.
  4. Initialize collectedGems = [], collectedExtraLives = [].
  5. Loop:
     a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol).
     b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break (movement ends at boundary).
     c. Get cell at nextPos.
     d. If cell is Wall, break (stop before Wall).
     e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break (stop exactly on StopCell).
     f. If cell is EntityCell:
        - If entity is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) (player stays at original position).
        - If entity is Gem: add nextPos to collectedGems.
        - If entity is ExtraLife: add nextPos to collectedExtraLives.
     g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue.
  6. After loop, if no movement occurred (currentPos unchanged from original), return Invalid.
  7. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell).
  8. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell (set entity to null).
  9. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.
  10. Return Alive(collectedGems, collectedExtraLives, newPosition=currentPos, origPosition=originalPos).
Related Features: gameBoard, gameBoard.player, gameBoard.board
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Position, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, ExtraLife, Mine, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell
Input: direction (Direction) - UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
Output: MoveResult - Alive, Dead, or Invalid.
Pre-condition: GameBoard is properly initialized with a player placed in a cell.
Post-condition: Player position updated for Alive/Dead; Gems/ExtraLives removed for Alive; board unchanged for Dead/Invalid.

GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverses a previous move, restoring the player position and any collected Gems/ExtraLives.
Algorithm:
  1. If prevMove is Alive:
     a. Move player back to prevMove.origPosition.
     b. For each position in prevMove.collectedGems, create a new Gem entity and place it in that cell.
     c. For each position in prevMove.collectedExtraLives, create a new ExtraLife entity and place it in that cell.
  2. If prevMove is Dead or Invalid, do nothing (Dead moves are not undoable).
Related Features: gameBoard, gameBoard.player
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, ExtraLife, Position
Input: prevMove (MoveResult) - the move to undo.
Output: void
Pre-condition: prevMove is a valid previous move (Alive) that was pushed to the stack.
Post-condition: Player position and board entities are restored to the state before the move.

This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary: Executes a move in the given direction using inertial sliding. Returns Alive, Dead, or Invalid depending on what happens during the slide.
Algorithm:
  1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction.
  2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position).
  3. If the immediate next cell in direction is out of bounds, Wall, or StopCell, return Invalid.
  4. Initialize collectedGems = [], collectedExtraLives = [].
  5. Loop:
     a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol).
     b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break (movement ends at boundary).
     c. Get cell at nextPos.
     d. If cell is Wall, break (stop before Wall).
     e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break (stop exactly on StopCell).
     f. If cell is EntityCell:
        - If entity is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) (player stays at original position).
        - If entity is Gem: add nextPos to collectedGems.
        - If entity is ExtraLife: add nextPos to collectedExtraLives.
     g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue.
  6. After loop, if no movement occurred (currentPos unchanged from original), return Invalid.
  7. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell).
  8. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell (set entity to null).
  9. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.
  10. Return Alive(collectedGems, collectedExtraLives, newPosition=currentPos, origPosition=originalPos).
Related Features: gameBoard, gameBoard.player, gameBoard.board
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Position, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, ExtraLife, Mine, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell
Input: direction (Direction) - UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
Output: MoveResult - Alive, Dead, or Invalid.
Pre-condition: GameBoard is properly initialized with a player placed in a cell.
Post-condition: Player position updated for Alive/Dead; Gems/ExtraLives removed for Alive; board unchanged for Dead/Invalid.

GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverses a previous move, restoring the player position and any collected Gems/ExtraLives.
Algorithm:
  1. If prevMove is Alive:
     a. Move player back to prevMove.origPosition.
     b. For each position in prevMove.collectedGems, create a new Gem entity and place it in that cell.
     c. For each position in prevMove.collectedExtraLives, create a new ExtraLife entity and place it in that cell.
  2. If prevMove is Dead or Invalid, do nothing (Dead moves are not undoable).
Related Features: gameBoard, gameBoard.player
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, ExtraLife, Position
Input: prevMove (MoveResult) - the move to undo.
Output: void
Pre-condition: prevMove is a valid previous move (Alive) that was pushed to the stack.
Post-condition: Player position and board entities are restored to the state before the move.

# Operation Specifications
EntityCell::setentity
Summary: Sets the Entity contained in this EntityCell. Updates the bidirectional relationship by clearing the old entity's owner reference and setting the new entity's owner.
Algorithm:
  1. If current entity exists and its owner is this, set old entity's owner to null.
  2. Set this.entity = newEntity.
  3. If newEntity is not null, set newEntity.owner = this.
Related Features: entity (EntityCell attribute)
Related Classes: Entity
Input: newEntity (Entity) - the new entity to place; can be null.
Output: Entity - the previous entity before the change.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The entity is updated; the old entity no longer references this cell; the new entity references this cell.

Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

# Operation Specifications
EntityCell::setentity
Summary: Sets the Entity contained in this EntityCell. Updates the bidirectional relationship by clearing the old entity's owner reference and setting the new entity's owner.
Algorithm:
  1. If current entity exists and its owner is this, set old entity's owner to null.
  2. Set this.entity = newEntity.
  3. If newEntity is not null, set newEntity.owner = this.
Related Features: entity (EntityCell attribute)
Related Classes: Entity
Input: newEntity (Entity) - the new entity to place; can be null.
Output: Entity - the previous entity before the change.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The entity is updated; the old entity no longer references this cell; the new entity references this cell.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top move. Increments popCount.
Algorithm:
  1. MoveResult top = moves.remove(moves.size()-1)
  2. popCount++
  3. return top
Related Features: moves, popCount
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the removed move.
Pre-condition: !isEmpty()
Post-condition: Stack size decreased by 1; popCount incremented.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the move stack has any moves.
Algorithm: return moves.isEmpty()
Related Features: moves (List<MoveResult>)
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if empty.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No side effects.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top move without removing it.
Algorithm: return moves.get(moves.size()-1)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None
Output: MoveResult - the top move.
Pre-condition: !isEmpty()
Post-condition: Stack unchanged.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Pushes a move onto the top of the stack.
Algorithm: moves.add(move)
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move (MoveResult) - the move to add.
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Stack size increased by 1; move is at top.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Position::offsetBy2
Summary: Returns a new Position offset by a PositionOffset.

Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset

Output: Position - new position.

Post-condition: Returns a new Position object; original unchanged.

Position::offsetByOrNull2
Summary: Same as offsetByOrNull1 but using a PositionOffset.
Algorithm: return offsetByOrNull1(offset.dRow, offset.dCol, numRows, numCols)
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input: offset (PositionOffset), numRows (int), numCols (int)
Output: Position or null
Pre-condition: numRows > 0, numCols > 0
Post-condition: Returns null or new Position; original unchanged.

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Returns a new Position offset by deltas if the result is within bounds; otherwise returns null.
Algorithm:
  newRow = row + dRow; newCol = col + dCol
  if newRow < 0 || newRow >= numRows || newCol < 0 || newCol >= numCols: return null
  return new Position(newRow, newCol)

Related Classes: Position

Post-condition: Returns null or new Position; original unchanged.
