# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Related Classes: GameBoard

Related Classes: None

Related Features: numLives

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Entity::setowner
Summary: Sets the owner EntityCell for this Entity. Updates the bidirectional relationship by replacing the entity reference in the old owner (if any) and the new owner.
Algorithm:
  1. If current owner exists and its entity is this, set old owner's entity to null.
  2. Set this.owner = newOwner.
  3. If newOwner is not null, set newOwner.entity = this.
Related Features: owner (Entity attribute)
Related Classes: EntityCell
Input: owner (EntityCell) - the new owner cell; can be null to detach.
Output: EntityCell - the previous owner cell before the change.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The owner is updated; the old owner no longer references this entity; the new owner references this entity.

The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns an entire column of cells as a list.
Algorithm: Iterate over all rows (0 to numRows-1) and collect board[row][col] into a list.
Related Features: board, numRows
Related Classes: Cell
Input: col (int) - 0-based column index, must be between 0 and numCols-1.
Output: List<Cell> - list of cells in that column, ordered top to bottom.
Pre-condition: col >= 0 && col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns a new list; no side effects.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Retrieves the Cell at the given Position.
Algorithm: Return board[position.row][position.col].
Related Features: board (CellArray2D), numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Position
Input: position (Position) - a valid position within the board.
Output: Cell - the cell at the given position.
Pre-condition: position.row >= 0 && position.row < numRows && position.col >= 0 && position.col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns the cell object; no side effects.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Retrieves the EntityCell at the given Position. Returns null if the cell is not an EntityCell.
Algorithm: Get cell at position; if cell is instance of EntityCell, return it; else return null.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: Position, EntityCell, Cell
Input: position (Position) - a valid position.
Output: EntityCell or null - the EntityCell at that position, or null if the cell is a Wall or StopCell.
Pre-condition: position is within board bounds.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns an entire row of cells as a list.
Algorithm: Iterate over all columns (0 to numCols-1) and collect board[row][col] into a list.
Related Features: board, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int) - 0-based row index, must be between 0 and numRows-1.
Output: List<Cell> - list of cells in that row, ordered left to right.
Pre-condition: row >= 0 && row < numRows
Post-condition: Returns a new list; no side effects.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Counts the number of Gem entities still present on the board.
Algorithm: Iterate through all cells; for each EntityCell, check if entity is instance of Gem; count them.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input: None
Output: int - the number of Gems remaining on the board.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Retrieves the EntityCell at the given row and column. Returns null if not an EntityCell.
Algorithm: Same as getEntityCell1 but using row/col indices.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: EntityCell, Cell
Input: row (int), col (int) - valid indices.
Output: EntityCell or null.
Pre-condition: row and col are within bounds.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Retrieves the Cell at the given row and column indices.
Algorithm: Return board[row][col] after validating indices.
Related Features: board (CellArray2D), numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int) - 0-based row index, must be between 0 and numRows-1; col (int) - 0-based column index, must be between 0 and numCols-1.
Output: Cell - the cell at the specified position.
Pre-condition: row >= 0 && row < numRows && col >= 0 && col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns the cell object; no side effects.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns an entire column of cells as a list.
Algorithm: Iterate over all rows (0 to numRows-1) and collect board[row][col] into a list.
Related Features: board, numRows
Related Classes: Cell
Input: col (int) - 0-based column index, must be between 0 and numCols-1.
Output: List<Cell> - list of cells in that column, ordered top to bottom.
Pre-condition: col >= 0 && col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns a new list; no side effects.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Retrieves the Cell at the given Position.
Algorithm: Return board[position.row][position.col].
Related Features: board (CellArray2D), numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Position
Input: position (Position) - a valid position within the board.
Output: Cell - the cell at the given position.
Pre-condition: position.row >= 0 && position.row < numRows && position.col >= 0 && position.col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns the cell object; no side effects.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Retrieves the EntityCell at the given Position. Returns null if the cell is not an EntityCell.
Algorithm: Get cell at position; if cell is instance of EntityCell, return it; else return null.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: Position, EntityCell, Cell
Input: position (Position) - a valid position.
Output: EntityCell or null - the EntityCell at that position, or null if the cell is a Wall (which is a Cell but not an EntityCell) or StopCell (which is an EntityCell, so this would return the StopCell).
Pre-condition: position is within board bounds.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns an entire row of cells as a list.
Algorithm: Iterate over all columns (0 to numCols-1) and collect board[row][col] into a list.
Related Features: board, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int) - 0-based row index, must be between 0 and numRows-1.
Output: List<Cell> - list of cells in that row, ordered left to right.
Pre-condition: row >= 0 && row < numRows
Post-condition: Returns a new list; no side effects.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Counts the number of Gem entities still present on the board.
Algorithm: Iterate through all EntityCells on the board; for each EntityCell, check if entity is instance of Gem; count them. Note: Only EntityCells can contain entities; Walls and StopCells do not contain Gems.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input: None
Output: int - the number of Gems remaining on the board.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Retrieves the EntityCell at the given row and column. Returns null if not an EntityCell.
Algorithm: Same as getEntityCell1 but using row/col indices.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: EntityCell, Cell
Input: row (int), col (int) - valid indices.
Output: EntityCell or null.
Pre-condition: row and col are within bounds.
Post-condition: No side effects.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Retrieves the Cell at the given row and column indices.
Algorithm: Return board[row][col] after validating indices.
Related Features: board (CellArray2D), numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int) - 0-based row index, must be between 0 and numRows-1; col (int) - 0-based column index, must be between 0 and numCols-1.
Output: Cell - the cell at the specified position.
Pre-condition: row >= 0 && row < numRows && col >= 0 && col < numCols
Post-condition: Returns the cell object; no side effects.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processMove
Summary: Processes a move command by delegating to GameBoardController.makeMove, then updates game state counters and stack accordingly.
Algorithm:
  1. Call gameState.getGameBoardController().makeMove(direction) -> result.
  2. If result is Invalid: do nothing, return result.
  3. If result is Dead:
     a. gameState.incrementNumMoves()
     b. gameState.incrementNumDeaths()
     c. If !gameState.hasUnlimitedLives(): gameState.decrementNumLives()
     d. Do NOT push to stack.
  4. If result is Alive:
     a. gameState.incrementNumMoves()
     b. For each ExtraLife in result.collectedExtraLives: gameState.increaseNumLives(1)
     c. Push result onto gameState.moveStack.
  5. Return result.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.gameBoardController, gameState.moveStack
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid
Input: direction (Direction) - the direction to move.
Output: MoveResult - the result from makeMove.
Pre-condition: gameState is initialized.
Post-condition: Counters updated; stack updated for Alive moves; lives decreased for Dead moves (finite lives).

GameController::processUndo
Summary: Attempts to undo the last Alive move. Returns true if successful, false if no moves to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. If gameState.moveStack.isEmpty(): return false.
  2. Pop move from gameState.moveStack.
  3. Call gameState.getGameBoardController().undoMove(move).
  4. For each ExtraLife in move.collectedExtraLives: gameState.decreaseNumLives(1) (reverse the gain).
  5. Return true.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.moveStack, gameState.gameBoardController
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack, GameBoardController, Alive, ExtraLife
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo performed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, player position and board restored; lives reversed; popCount incremented.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

      for (int col = 0; col < getNumCols(); col++) {
        Cell cell = getBoard()[row][col];
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell) {
          Entity entity = ((EntityCell) cell).getEntity();
          if (entity instanceof Gem) {
            count++;
          }
        }
      }
    }
    return count;
  }

   *   score = (numRows * numCols) + (collectedGems * 10) - (numMoves * 1) - (moveStack.popCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4)

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

  {

      // do nothing
    } else if (result instanceof Dead) {
      gameState.incrementNumMoves();
      gameState.incrementNumDeaths();
      if (!gameState.hasUnlimitedLives()) {
        gameState.decrementNumLives();
      }
      // Do NOT push to stack

        gameState.increaseNumLives(1);
      }
      gameState.getMoveStack().push(result);
    }
    
    return result;
  }

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Executes a move in the given direction using inertial sliding. Returns Alive, Dead, or Invalid depending on what happens during the slide.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction.
   *   2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position).
   *   3. Set originalPos = currentPos.
   *   4. Loop:
   *      a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol).
   *      b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break (movement ends at boundary).
   *      c. Get cell at nextPos.
   *      d. If cell is Wall, break (stop before Wall).
   *      e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break (stop exactly on StopCell).
   *      f. If cell is EntityCell:
   *         - If entity is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) (player stays at original position, no collection).
   *         - If entity is Gem: add nextPos to collectedGems.
   *         - If entity is ExtraLife: add nextPos to collectedExtraLives.
   *      g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue.
   *   5. After loop, if no movement occurred (currentPos unchanged from original), return Invalid.
   *   6. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell).
   *   7. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell (set entity to null).
   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.

   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.

public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
{
    // Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction
    int dRow = 0;
    int dCol = 0;
    switch (direction.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            dRow = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            dRow = 1;
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            dCol = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            dCol = 1;
            break;
    }
    
    // Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position)
    Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
    EntityCell playerOwner = player.getOwner();
    Position currentPos = playerOwner.getPosition();
    Position originalPos = currentPos;
    
    EList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<Position>();
    EList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<Position>();
    
    int numRows = gameBoard.getNumRows();
    int numCols = gameBoard.getNumCols();
    
    // Loop
    while (true) {
        // Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol)
        Position nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy1(dRow, dCol);
        
        // If nextPos is out of bounds, break
        if (nextPos == null) {
            break;
        }
        int nextRow = nextPos.getRow();
        int nextCol = nextPos.getCol();
        if (nextRow < 0 || nextRow >= numRows || nextCol < 0 || nextCol >= numCols) {
            break;
        }
        
        // Get cell at nextPos
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos);
        
        // If cell is Wall, break
        if (cell instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        
        // If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            currentPos = nextPos;
            break;
        }
        
        // If cell is EntityCell
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell) {
            EntityCell entityCell = (EntityCell) cell;
            Entity entity = entityCell.getEntity();
            
            if (entity instanceof Mine) {
                // Return Dead
                Dead deadResult = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createDead();
                deadResult.setMinePosition(nextPos);
                return deadResult;
            } else if (entity instanceof Gem) {
                collectedGems.add(nextPos);
            } else if (entity instanceof ExtraLife) {
                collectedExtraLives.add(nextPos);
            }
        }
        
        // Set currentPos = nextPos; continue
        currentPos = nextPos;
    }
    
    // After loop, if no movement occurred, return Invalid
    if (currentPos.getRow() == originalPos.getRow() && currentPos.getCol() == originalPos.getCol()) {
        Invalid invalidResult = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalid();
        return invalidResult;
    }
    
    // Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell)
    Cell targetCell = gameBoard.getCell2(currentPos);
    if (targetCell instanceof EntityCell) {
        EntityCell targetEntityCell = (EntityCell) targetCell;
        playerOwner.setEntity(null);
        targetEntityCell.setEntity(player);
        player.setOwner(targetEntityCell);
    }
    
    // For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell
    for (Position gemPos : collectedGems) {
        EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(gemPos);
        if (gemCell != null) {
            gemCell.setEntity(null);
        }
    }
    
    // For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell
    for (Position lifePos : collectedExtraLives) {
        EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(lifePos);
        if (lifeCell != null) {
            lifeCell.setEntity(null);
        }
    }
    
    // Return Alive
    Alive aliveResult = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createAlive();
    aliveResult.getCollectedGems().addAll(collectedGems);
    aliveResult.getCollectedExtraLives().addAll(collectedExtraLives);
    aliveResult.setNewPosition(currentPos);
    aliveResult.setOrigPosition(originalPos);
    return aliveResult;
}
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (prevMove instanceof Alive) {
        Alive aliveMove = (Alive) prevMove;
        
        // Move player back to prevMove.origPosition
        Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
        Position origPos = aliveMove.getOrigPosition();
        EntityCell origCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(origPos);
        
        // Remove player from current cell
        EntityCell currentOwner = player.getOwner();
        if (currentOwner != null) {
            currentOwner.setEntity(null);
        }
        
        // Place player in original cell
        if (origCell != null) {
            origCell.setEntity(player);
            player.setOwner(origCell);
        }
        
        // For each position in collectedGems, create a new Gem and place it
        for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
            EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(gemPos);
            if (gemCell != null) {
                Gem gem = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createGem();
                gemCell.setEntity(gem);
                gem.setOwner(gemCell);
            }
        }
        
        // For each position in collectedExtraLives, create a new ExtraLife and place it
        for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
            EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(lifePos);
            if (lifeCell != null) {
                ExtraLife extraLife = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createExtraLife();
                lifeCell.setEntity(extraLife);
                extraLife.setOwner(lifeCell);
            }
        }
    }
    // If prevMove is Dead or Invalid, do nothing
}
public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
{
    // 1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction
    int dRow = 0;
    int dCol = 0;
    switch (direction.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            dRow = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            dRow = 1;
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            dCol = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            dCol = 1;
            break;
    }
    
    // 2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position)
    Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
    Position currentPos = player.getOwner().getPosition();
    // 3. Set originalPos = currentPos
    Position originalPos = currentPos;
    
    // Collected lists
    EList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<Position>();
    EList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<Position>();
    
    int numRows = gameBoard.getNumRows();
    int numCols = gameBoard.getNumCols();
    
    // 4. Loop
    while (true) {
        // a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol)
        Position nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy1(dRow, dCol);
        int nextRow = nextPos.getRow();
        int nextCol = nextPos.getCol();
        
        // b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break
        if (nextRow < 0 || nextRow >= numRows || nextCol < 0 || nextCol >= numCols) {
            break;
        }
        
        // c. Get cell at nextPos
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell1(nextRow, nextCol);
        
        // d. If cell is Wall, break
        if (cell instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        
        // e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            currentPos = nextPos;
            break;
        }
        
        // f. If cell is EntityCell
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell) {
            EntityCell entityCell = (EntityCell) cell;
            Entity entity = entityCell.getEntity();
            if (entity instanceof Mine) {
                // Return Dead
                Dead dead = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createDead();
                dead.setMinePosition(nextPos);
                return dead;
            } else if (entity instanceof Gem) {
                collectedGems.add(nextPos);
            } else if (entity instanceof ExtraLife) {
                collectedExtraLives.add(nextPos);
            }
        }
        
        // g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue
        currentPos = nextPos;
    }
    
    // 5. If no movement occurred, return Invalid
    if (currentPos.getRow() == originalPos.getRow() && currentPos.getCol() == originalPos.getCol()) {
        return Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalid();
    }
    
    // 6. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell)
    EntityCell targetCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(currentPos.getRow(), currentPos.getCol());
    if (targetCell != null) {
        player.getOwner().setEntity(null);
        targetCell.setEntity(player);
        player.setOwner(targetCell);
    }
    
    // 7. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell
    for (Position gemPos : collectedGems) {
        EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(gemPos.getRow(), gemPos.getCol());
        if (gemCell != null) {
            gemCell.setEntity(null);
        }
    }
    
    // 8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell
    for (Position lifePos : collectedExtraLives) {
        EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(lifePos.getRow(), lifePos.getCol());
        if (lifeCell != null) {
            lifeCell.setEntity(null);
        }
    }
    
    // 9. Return Alive
    Alive alive = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createAlive();
    alive.getCollectedGems().addAll(collectedGems);
    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().addAll(collectedExtraLives);
    alive.setNewPosition(currentPos);
    alive.setOrigPosition(originalPos);
    return alive;
}
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove)
{
    // 1. If prevMove is Alive
    if (prevMove instanceof Alive) {
        Alive aliveMove = (Alive) prevMove;
        
        // a. Move player back to prevMove.origPosition
        Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
        Position origPos = aliveMove.getOrigPosition();
        EntityCell origCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(origPos.getRow(), origPos.getCol());
        if (origCell != null) {
            // Remove player from current cell
            EntityCell currentOwner = player.getOwner();
            if (currentOwner != null) {
                currentOwner.setEntity(null);
            }
            // Place player in original cell
            origCell.setEntity(player);
            player.setOwner(origCell);
        }
        
        // b. For each position in collectedGems, create a new Gem entity and place it
        for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
            EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(gemPos.getRow(), gemPos.getCol());
            if (gemCell != null) {
                Gem gem = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createGem();
                gemCell.setEntity(gem);
                gem.setOwner(gemCell);
            }
        }
        
        // c. For each position in collectedExtraLives, create a new ExtraLife entity and place it
        for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
            EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell2(lifePos.getRow(), lifePos.getCol());
            if (lifeCell != null) {
                ExtraLife extraLife = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createExtraLife();
                lifeCell.setEntity(extraLife);
                extraLife.setOwner(lifeCell);
            }
        }
    }
    // 2. If prevMove is Dead or Invalid, do nothing
}

   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction.
   *   2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position).
   *   3. Set originalPos = currentPos.
   *   4. Loop:
   *      a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol).
   *      b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break (movement ends at boundary).
   *      c. Get cell at nextPos.
   *      d. If cell is Wall, break (stop before Wall).
   *      e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break (stop exactly on StopCell).
   *      f. If cell is EntityCell:
   *         - If entity is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) (player stays at original position, no collection).
   *         - If entity is Gem: add nextPos to collectedGems.
   *         - If entity is ExtraLife: add nextPos to collectedExtraLives.
   *      g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue.
   *   5. After loop, if no movement occurred (currentPos unchanged from original), return Invalid.
   *   6. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell).
   *   7. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell (set entity to null).
   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.
   *   9. Return Alive(collectedGems, collectedExtraLives, newPosition=currentPos, origPosition=originalPos).

   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.

   * Summary: Executes a move in the given direction using inertial sliding. Returns Alive, Dead, or Invalid depending on what happens during the slide.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction.
   *   2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position).
   *   3. Set originalPos = currentPos.
   *   4. Loop:
   *      a. Compute nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy(dRow, dCol).
   *      b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break (movement ends at boundary).
   *      c. Get cell at nextPos.
   *      d. If cell is Wall, break (stop before Wall).
   *      e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break (stop exactly on StopCell).
   *      f. If cell is EntityCell:
   *         - If entity is Mine: return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) (player stays at original position, no collection).
   *         - If entity is Gem: add nextPos to collectedGems.
   *         - If entity is ExtraLife: add nextPos to collectedExtraLives.
   *      g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue.
   *   5. After loop, if no movement occurred (currentPos unchanged from original), return Invalid.
   *   6. Move player entity to currentPos (update owner cell).
   *   7. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell (set entity to null).
   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.
   *   9. Return Alive(collectedGems, collectedExtraLives, newPosition=currentPos, origPosition=originalPos).
   * Related Features: gameBoard, gameBoard.player, gameBoard.board
   * Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Position, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, ExtraLife, Mine, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell
   * Input: direction (Direction) - UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
   * Output: MoveResult - Alive, Dead, or Invalid.
   * Pre-condition: GameBoard is properly initialized with a player placed in a cell.
   * Post-condition: For Alive: player position updated, Gems/ExtraLives passed through are removed from board. For Dead: board unchanged, player stays at original position. For Invalid: board unchanged.

   *   8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell.

For `makeMove`:

```java
public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
    // 1. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from Direction
    int dRow = 0, dCol = 0;
    switch (direction.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            dRow = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            dRow = 1;
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            dCol = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            dCol = 1;
            break;
    }
    
    // 2. Set currentPos = gameBoard.player's position (owner.position)
    GameBoard gameBoard = getGameBoard();
    Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
    Position currentPos = player.getOwner().getPosition();
    Position originalPos = currentPos;
    
    // Collections for collected items
    EList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<Position>();
    EList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<Position>();
    
    // 4. Loop
    int numRows = gameBoard.getNumRows();
    int numCols = gameBoard.getNumCols();
    
    while (true) {
        // a. Compute nextPos
        Position nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy1(dRow, dCol);
        
        // b. If nextPos is out of bounds, break
        if (nextPos.getRow() < 0 || nextPos.getRow() >= numRows || nextPos.getCol() < 0 || nextPos.getCol() >= numCols) {
            break;
        }
        
        // c. Get cell at nextPos
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell1(nextPos.getRow(), nextPos.getCol());
        
        // d. If cell is Wall, break
        if (cell instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        
        // e. If cell is StopCell, set currentPos = nextPos; break
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            currentPos = nextPos;
            break;
        }
        
        // f. If cell is EntityCell
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell) {
            EntityCell entityCell = (EntityCell) cell;
            Entity entity = entityCell.getEntity();
            if (entity != null) {
                if (entity instanceof Mine) {
                    // Return Dead(minePosition=nextPos) - player stays at original position
                    Dead dead = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createDead();
                    dead.setMinePosition(nextPos);
                    return dead;
                } else if (entity instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(nextPos);
                } else if (entity instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(nextPos);
                }
            }
        }
        
        // g. Set currentPos = nextPos; continue
        currentPos = nextPos;
    }
    
    // 5. After loop, if no movement occurred, return Invalid
    if (currentPos == originalPos || (currentPos.getRow() == originalPos.getRow() && currentPos.getCol() == originalPos.getCol())) {
        return Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalid();
    }
    
    // 6. Move player entity to currentPos
    EntityCell targetCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(currentPos);
    EntityCell oldCell = player.getOwner();
    oldCell.setEntity(null);
    player.setOwner(targetCell);
    // EMF inverse should handle setting targetCell's entity
    
    // 7. For each collectedGem position, remove Gem entity from that cell
    for (Position gemPos : collectedGems) {
        EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(gemPos);
        gemCell.setEntity(null);
    }
    
    // 8. For each collectedExtraLife position, remove ExtraLife entity from that cell
    for (Position lifePos : collectedExtraLives) {
        EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(lifePos);
        lifeCell.setEntity(null);
    }
    
    // 9. Return Alive
    Alive alive = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createAlive();
    alive.setOrigPosition(originalPos);
    alive.setNewPosition(currentPos);
    alive.getCollectedGems().addAll(collectedGems);
    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().addAll(collectedExtraLives);
    return alive;
}
```

For `undoMove`:

```java
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (prevMove instanceof Alive) {
        Alive aliveMove = (Alive) prevMove;
        GameBoard gameBoard = getGameBoard();
        Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
        
        // a. Move player back to prevMove.origPosition
        Position origPos = aliveMove.getOrigPosition();
        EntityCell origCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(origPos);
        EntityCell currentCell = player.getOwner();
        currentCell.setEntity(null);
        player.setOwner(origCell);
        
        // b. For each position in collectedGems, create a new Gem and place it
        for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
            EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(gemPos);
            Gem gem = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createGem();
            gemCell.setEntity(gem);
        }
        
        // c. For each position in collectedExtraLives, create a new ExtraLife and place it
        for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
            EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(lifePos);
            ExtraLife extraLife = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createExtraLife();
            lifeCell.setEntity(extraLife);
        }
    }
    // 2. If prevMove is Dead or Invalid, do nothing
}

public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
    // 1. Determine delta
    int dRow = 0, dCol = 0;
    switch (direction.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            dRow = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            dRow = 1;
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            dCol = -1;
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            dCol = 1;
            break;
    }
    
    GameBoard gameBoard = getGameBoard();
    Player player = gameBoard.getPlayer();
    Position currentPos = player.getOwner().getPosition();
    Position originalPos = currentPos;
    
    EList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<Position>();
    EList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<Position>();
    
    int numRows = gameBoard.getNumRows();
    int numCols = gameBoard.getNumCols();
    
    while (true) {
        Position nextPos = currentPos.offsetBy1(dRow, dCol);
        
        if (nextPos.getRow() < 0 || nextPos.getRow() >= numRows || nextPos.getCol() < 0 || nextPos.getCol() >= numCols) {
            break;
        }
        
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell1(nextPos.getRow(), nextPos.getCol());
        
        if (cell instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            currentPos = nextPos;
            break;
        }
        
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell) {
            EntityCell entityCell = (EntityCell) cell;
            Entity entity = entityCell.getEntity();
            if (entity instanceof Mine) {
                Dead dead = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createDead();
                dead.setMinePosition(nextPos);
                return dead;
            } else if (entity instanceof Gem) {
                collectedGems.add(nextPos);
            } else if (entity instanceof ExtraLife) {
                collectedExtraLives.add(nextPos);
            }
        }
        
        currentPos = nextPos;
    }
    
    if (currentPos.getRow() == originalPos.getRow() && currentPos.getCol() == originalPos.getCol()) {
        return Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createInvalid();
    }
    
    // Move player to currentPos
    EntityCell targetCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(currentPos);
    player.setOwner(targetCell);
    
    // Remove collected gems
    for (Position gemPos : collectedGems) {
        EntityCell gemCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(gemPos);
        gemCell.setEntity(null);
    }
    
    // Remove collected extra lives
    for (Position lifePos : collectedExtraLives) {
        EntityCell lifeCell = gameBoard.getEntityCell1(lifePos);
        lifeCell.setEntity(null);
    }
    
    Alive alive = Pa21Factory.eINSTANCE.createAlive();
    alive.setOrigPosition(originalPos);
    alive.setNewPosition(currentPos);
    alive.getCollectedGems().addAll(collectedGems);
    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().addAll(collectedExtraLives);
    return alive;
}

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

The player slides until hitting a Wall, boundary, StopCell, or Mine. Returns the MoveResult.
Algorithm:
  1. Get player's current position from gameBoard.player.owner.position. Store as originalPosition.
  2. Determine delta (dRow, dCol) from direction: UP(-1,0), DOWN(1,0), LEFT(0,-1), RIGHT(0,1).
  3. Set currentPos = originalPosition.
  4. Set moved = false.
  5. Loop:
     a. Calculate nextPos = currentPos.offsetByOrNull1(dRow, dCol, numRows, numCols).
     b. If nextPos is null (out of bounds): break. Mark moved = true if any step taken.
     c. Get nextCell = gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos).
     d. If nextCell is Wall: break. Mark moved = true if any step taken.
     e. If nextCell is StopCell: set currentPos = nextPos; moved = true; break.
     f. If nextCell is EntityCell:
        i.   If entity is Mine: return new Dead(originalPosition, minePosition=nextPos). No changes to board.
        ii.  If entity is Gem: record nextPos in collectedGems list; remove entity from cell.
        iii. If entity is ExtraLife: record nextPos in collectedExtraLives list; remove entity from cell.
        iv.  (Player entity not encountered during slide as player is only in starting cell or StopCell)
     g. Set currentPos = nextPos; moved = true.
  6. If not moved: return new Invalid(originalPosition).
  7. Move player entity to currentPos cell:
     a. Remove player from original cell (set entity to null).
     b. Place player in currentPos cell (call setentity on the target EntityCell).
  8. Return new Alive(currentPos, originalPosition, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives).

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processMove
Summary: Processes a move through the game controller, updating game state counters and the move stack.
Algorithm:
  1. Call gameState.gameBoardController.makeMove(direction) to get result.
  2. If result is Invalid: return result (no counters changed, no push to stack).
  3. If result is Dead:
     a. Call gameState.incrementNumMoves().
     b. Call gameState.incrementNumDeaths().
     c. If not gameState.hasUnlimitedLives(): call gameState.decrementNumLives().
     d. Do NOT push to moveStack.
     e. Return result.
  4. If result is Alive:
     a. Call gameState.incrementNumMoves().
     b. For each ExtraLife in result.collectedExtraLives: call gameState.increaseNumLives(1).
     c. Push result to gameState.moveStack.
     d. Return result.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.gameBoardController, gameState.moveStack
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid
Input:
  - direction: Direction - the direction to move
Output: MoveResult - the result of the move
Pre-condition: gameState is initialized with a valid game board and player.
Post-condition:
  - Invalid: no state changes.
  - Dead: numMoves incremented, numDeaths incremented, numLives decremented if not unlimited.
  - Alive: numMoves incremented, ExtraLives collected increase numLives, move pushed to stack.

GameController::processUndo
Summary: Attempts to undo the most recent Alive move. Returns true if successful, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If gameState.moveStack.isEmpty(): return false.
  2. Pop the top move from moveStack: prevMove = gameState.moveStack.pop().
  3. Call gameState.gameBoardController.undoMove(prevMove).
  4. If prevMove is Alive:
     a. For each ExtraLife collected in prevMove.collectedExtraLives: call gameState.decreaseNumLives(1).
  5. Increment moveStack.popCount.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.moveStack, gameState.gameBoardController
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive, ExtraLife, Position
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if an undo was performed, false if no moves to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition:
  - If false: no changes.
  - If true: player position restored, collected Gems/ExtraLives restored, ExtraLife gains reversed, popCount incremented.

     e. Return result.
  4. If result is Alive:
     a. Call gameState.incrementNumMoves().
     b. For each ExtraLife in result.collectedExtraLives: call gameState.increaseNumLives(1).
     c. Push result to gameState.moveStack.
     d. Return result.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.gameBoardController, gameState.moveStack
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid
Input:
  - direction: Direction - the direction to move
Output: MoveResult - the result of the move
Pre-condition: gameState is initialized with a valid game board and player.
Post-condition:
  - Invalid: no state changes.
  - Dead: numMoves incremented, numDeaths incremented, numLives decremented if not unlimited.
  - Alive: numMoves incremented, ExtraLives collected increase numLives, move pushed to stack.

GameController::processUndo
Summary: Attempts to undo the most recent Alive move. Returns true if successful, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If gameState.moveStack.isEmpty(): return false.
  2. Pop the top move from moveStack: prevMove = gameState.moveStack.pop().
  3. Call gameState.gameBoardController.undoMove(prevMove).
  4. If prevMove is Alive:
     a. For each ExtraLife collected in prevMove.collectedExtraLives: call gameState.decreaseNumLives(1).
  5. Increment moveStack.popCount.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: gameState, gameState.moveStack, gameState.gameBoardController
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive, ExtraLife, Position
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if an undo was performed, false if no moves to undo
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition:
  - If false: no changes.
  - If true: player position restored, collected Gems/ExtraLives restored, ExtraLife gains reversed, popCount incremented.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```
